question: In Daniel 1:1-2, in which year of Jehoiakim king of Judah did Nebuchadnezzar come against Jerusalem, and to what land and house did he carry part of the vessels of the house of God?

opt3: In the eleventh year of Zedekiah; carried into the city of Babylon to the shrine of Bel

question: In Daniel 2:1-4, in which year of Nebuchadnezzar's reign did he have troubling dreams, and in what language did the Chaldeans address the king from verse 4 onward?

explanation: Daniel 2:10-11 (KJV) - "The Chaldeans answered before the king, and said, There is not a man upon the earth that can shew the king's matter: therefore there is no king, lord, nor ruler, that asked such things at any magician, or astrologer, or Chaldean. And it is a rare thing that the king requireth, and there is none other that can shew it before the king, except the gods, whose dwelling is not with flesh."

correct: Arioch; Daniel answered with counsel and wisdom, and went in to request that the king give him time to show the interpretation
explanation: Daniel 2:14-16 (KJV) - "Then Daniel answered with counsel and wisdom to Arioch the captain of the king's guard, which was gone forth to slay the wise men of Babylon: He answered and said to Arioch the king's captain, Why is the decree so hasty from the king? Then Arioch made the thing known to Daniel. Then Daniel went in, and desired of the king that he would give him time, and that he would shew the king the interpretation."

question: In Daniel 2:27-30, how did Daniel disclaim any personal wisdom or superiority when brought before Nebuchadnezzar by Arioch?

question: In Daniel 3:19-22, to what degree did Nebuchadnezzar command the furnace to be heated, and what consequence befell the mighty men who threw the three youths into the fire?

question: What sight caused King Nebuchadnezzar to rise up in astonishment and question his counsellors in Daniel 3:24-25?

question: According to Daniel 3:26-27, what was verified about the physical condition and garments of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego when they came out of the furnace?

question: In Daniel 3:28-29, what royal decree did Nebuchadnezzar issue regarding anyone who should speak amiss against the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego?

opt3: He decreed that the name of Bel should be exalted above all gods throughout the four quarters of the earth
opt4: He thought it good to shew the signs and wonders that the high God had wrought toward him: "How great are his signs! and how mighty are his wonders! his kingdom is an everlasting kingdom"
correct: He thought it good to shew the signs and wonders that the high God had wrought toward him: "How great are his signs! and how mighty are his wonders! his kingdom is an everlasting kingdom"
explanation: Daniel 4:2-3 (KJV) - "I thought it good to shew the signs and wonders that the high God hath wrought toward me. How great are his signs! and how mighty are his wonders! his kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and his dominion is from generation to generation."

question: In Daniel 4:10-12, what description is given of the great tree in the midst of the earth seen in Nebuchadnezzar's vision?
opt1: Its height reached unto heaven and the sight thereof to the end of all the earth; the leaves fair, fruit much, giving shadow to beasts and food for all flesh
opt2: A mighty cedar of Lebanon whose roots reached Sheol and whose branches darkened the sun, yet bare no fruit
opt3: A spreading olive tree planted by the river Euphrates, bearing golden olives and sheltering all the flocks of Chaldea
opt4: A great vine extending from Babylon to Jerusalem, whose grapes produced royal wine for all nations
correct: Its height reached unto heaven and the sight thereof to the end of all the earth; the leaves fair, fruit much, giving shadow to beasts and food for all flesh
explanation: Daniel 4:10-12 (KJV) - "Thus were the visions of mine head in my bed; I saw, and behold a tree in the midst of the earth, and the height thereof was great. The tree grew, and was strong, and the height thereof reached unto heaven, and the sight thereof to the end of all the earth: The leaves thereof were fair, and the fruit thereof much, and in it was meat for all: the beasts of the field had shadow under it, and the fowls of the heaven dwelt in the boughs thereof, and all flesh was fed of it."

question: According to Daniel 4:13-16, who descended from heaven to pronounce judgment upon the tree, and what was commanded regarding its stump and heart?
opt1: An archangel with a flaming sword commanded to uproot the tree entirely and burn it to ashes with unquenchable fire
opt2: A watcher and an holy one cried aloud to hew down the tree, but leave the stump with a band of iron and brass; and let his heart be changed from man's to a beast's, and let seven times pass over him
opt3: The spirit of Marduk ordered the branches lopped off, but the trunk preserved until forty days of mourning had elapsed
opt4: A seraph proclaimed that the tree should be transplanted into the wilderness of Shinar to wither under the scorching wind
correct: A watcher and an holy one cried aloud to hew down the tree, but leave the stump with a band of iron and brass; and let his heart be changed from man's to a beast's, and let seven times pass over him
explanation: Daniel 4:13, 15-16 (KJV) - "I saw in the visions of my head upon my bed, and, behold, a watcher and an holy one came down from heaven ... Nevertheless leave the stump of his roots in the earth, even with a band of iron and brass, in the tender grass of the field; and let it be wet with the dew of heaven, and let his portion be with the beasts in the grass of the earth: Let his heart be changed from man's, and let a beast's heart be given unto him; and let seven times pass over him."

question: What supreme divine purpose of the decree of the watchers is declared in Daniel 4:17?
opt1: That all nations may recognize the military supremacy of the Medes and Persians over Babylon
opt2: That the temple vessels carried from Jerusalem might be sanctified and restored by an earthly king
opt3: To the intent that the living may know that the most High ruleth in the kingdom of men, and giveth it to whomsoever he will, and setteth up over it the basest of men
opt4: That the wise men and astrologers of Chaldea may confess their total ignorance of heavenly decrees
correct: To the intent that the living may know that the most High ruleth in the kingdom of men, and giveth it to whomsoever he will, and setteth up over it the basest of men
explanation: Daniel 4:17 (KJV) - "This matter is by the decree of the watchers, and the demand by the word of the holy ones: to the intent that the living may know that the most High ruleth in the kingdom of men, and giveth it to whomsoever he will, and setteth up over it the basest of men."

question: In Daniel 4:19, how did Daniel (Belteshazzar) respond when he comprehended the terrifying meaning of the dream?
opt1: He wept aloud before the court and fell upon his face, refusing to speak until the king comforted him
opt2: He rejoiced that the righteous judgment of God was finally coming upon the oppressor of Judah
opt3: He immediately demanded that Nebuchadnezzar abdicate the throne and put on sackcloth
opt4: He was astonied for one hour, and his thoughts troubled him; and he said, "My lord, the dream be to them that hate thee, and the interpretation thereof to thine enemies"
correct: He was astonied for one hour, and his thoughts troubled him; and he said, "My lord, the dream be to them that hate thee, and the interpretation thereof to thine enemies"
explanation: Daniel 4:19 (KJV) - "Then Daniel, whose name was Belteshazzar, was astonied for one hour, and his thoughts troubled him. The king spake, and said, Belteshazzar, let not the dream, or the interpretation thereof, trouble thee. Belteshazzar answered and said, My lord, the dream be to them that hate thee, and the interpretation thereof to thine enemies."

question: According to Daniel 4:20-26, how did Daniel interpret the tree, the cutting down, and the stump remaining in the ground?
opt1: The tree is Nebuchadnezzar who has grown great; he shall be driven from men to eat grass as oxen for seven times, yet his kingdom shall be sure unto him after he knows that the heavens do rule
opt2: The tree is the city of Babylon which shall be burned by Cyrus, yet its ruins will be rebuilt after seventy years
opt3: The tree is the dynasty of Chaldea which shall be divided among four generals, yet retain its ancient laws
opt4: The tree is the royal palace which shall collapse in an earthquake, yet the king's lineage will be spared
correct: The tree is Nebuchadnezzar who has grown great; he shall be driven from men to eat grass as oxen for seven times, yet his kingdom shall be sure unto him after he knows that the heavens do rule
explanation: Daniel 4:22, 25-26 (KJV) - "It is thou, O king, that art grown and become strong ... That they shall drive thee from men, and thy dwelling shall be with the beasts of the field, and they shall make thee to eat grass as oxen, and they shall wet thee with the dew of heaven, and seven times shall pass over thee, till thou know that the most High ruleth in the kingdom of men, and giveth it to whomsoever he will. And whereas they commanded to leave the stump of the tree roots; thy kingdom shall be sure unto thee, after that thou shalt have known that the heavens do rule."

question: What urgent moral counsel did Daniel give to King Nebuchadnezzar in Daniel 4:27 to lengthen his tranquility?
opt1: Offer a thousand bullocks upon the altar of God in Jerusalem, and release all Hebrew captives
opt2: "Break off thy sins by righteousness, and thine iniquities by shewing mercy to the poor; if it may be a lengthening of thy tranquillity"
opt3: Build seven hospitals in Babylon and feed the orphans of the empire for three years
opt4: Destroy all the idols of gold and silver in the temple of Bel, and appoint Daniel as supreme ruler
correct: "Break off thy sins by righteousness, and thine iniquities by shewing mercy to the poor; if it may be a lengthening of thy tranquillity"
explanation: Daniel 4:27 (KJV) - "Wherefore, O king, let my counsel be acceptable unto thee, and break off thy sins by righteousness, and thine iniquities by shewing mercy to the poor; if it may be a lengthening of thy tranquillity."

question: In Daniel 4:29-31, what boast was Nebuchadnezzar uttering while walking in the palace of the kingdom twelve months later, immediately before a voice fell from heaven?
opt1: "Behold the walls and hanging gardens which no earthly army can ever breach or overthrow!"
opt2: "Who among the gods of heaven can challenge my sovereign dominion or alter my royal decrees?"
opt3: "Is not this great Babylon, that I have built for the house of the kingdom by the might of my power, and for the honour of my majesty?"
opt4: "My throne is established forever, and all nations under heaven shall bow beneath my feet!"
correct: "Is not this great Babylon, that I have built for the house of the kingdom by the might of my power, and for the honour of my majesty?"
explanation: Daniel 4:30-31 (KJV) - "The king spake, and said, Is not this great Babylon, that I have built for the house of the kingdom by the might of my power, and for the honour of my majesty? While the word was in the king's mouth, there fell a voice from heaven, saying, O king Nebuchadnezzar, to thee it is spoken; The kingdom is departed from thee."

question: According to Daniel 4:33, what was the exact fulfillment of the judgment upon Nebuchadnezzar the same hour?
opt1: He was struck with sudden blindness, cast into a remote fortress, and fed on husks for seven months
opt2: He wandered into the Zagros mountains, roaring like a wounded lion, until his royal robes rotted away
opt3: He lost the power of speech, burrowed into the earth like a badger, and was forgotten by his nobles
opt4: He was driven from men, did eat grass as oxen, his body was wet with the dew of heaven, till his hairs were grown like eagles' feathers, and his nails like birds' claws
correct: He was driven from men, did eat grass as oxen, his body was wet with the dew of heaven, till his hairs were grown like eagles' feathers, and his nails like birds' claws
explanation: Daniel 4:33 (KJV) - "The same hour was the thing fulfilled upon Nebuchadnezzar: and he was driven from men, and did eat grass as oxen, and his body was wet with the dew of heaven, till his hairs were grown like eagles' feathers, and his nails like birds' claws."

question: In Daniel 4:34-37, what did Nebuchadnezzar do at the end of the days that restored his understanding and kingdom, and what was his concluding testimony?
opt1: He lifted up his eyes unto heaven, praised and honoured the most High who liveth for ever, whose works are truth and ways judgment, and who is able to abase those that walk in pride
opt2: He made a pilgrimage to the ruins of Jerusalem, confessing his sins, and was restored by the prophet Jeremiah
opt3: He built a golden sanctuary for the God of heaven in Babylon, decreeing capital punishment for any idolater
opt4: He abdicated his throne in favor of Daniel and lived his remaining years as a solitary hermit in the desert
correct: He lifted up his eyes unto heaven, praised and honoured the most High who liveth for ever, whose works are truth and ways judgment, and who is able to abase those that walk in pride
explanation: Daniel 4:34, 37 (KJV) - "And at the end of the days I Nebuchadnezzar lifted up mine eyes unto heaven, and mine understanding returned unto me, and I blessed the most High, and I praised and honoured him that liveth for ever ... Now I Nebuchadnezzar praise and extol and honour the King of heaven, all whose works are truth, and his ways judgment: and those that walk in pride he is able to abase."

question: In Daniel 5:1-4, who made a great feast to a thousand of his lords, and what sacrilegious act did he commit with the temple vessels?
opt1: Belshazzar the king; he drank wine from the golden and silver vessels taken out of the temple of Jerusalem, and praised gods of gold, silver, brass, iron, wood, and stone
opt2: Evilmerodach; he melted down the sacred vessels of Jerusalem to cast an idol of the moon god Sin
opt3: Nabonidus; he gave the holy vessels to the temple prostitutes during the feast of Ishtar
opt4: Neriglissar; he filled the golden censers with swine's blood to mock the God of Judah
correct: Belshazzar the king; he drank wine from the golden and silver vessels taken out of the temple of Jerusalem, and praised gods of gold, silver, brass, iron, wood, and stone
explanation: Daniel 5:1-4 (KJV) - "Belshazzar the king made a great feast to a thousand of his lords, and drank wine before the thousand. Belshazzar, whiles he tasted the wine, commanded to bring the golden and silver vessels which his father Nebuchadnezzar had taken out of the temple which was in Jerusalem; that the king, and his princes, his wives, and his concubines, might drink therein ... They drank wine, and praised the gods of gold, and of silver, of brass, of iron, of wood, and of stone."

question: According to Daniel 5:5-6, what terrifying sight appeared in the banquet hall, and what physical effect did it produce on Belshazzar?
opt1: A pillar of fire emerged from the floor and inscribed flaming letters; the king fell unconscious and foamed at the mouth
opt2: Fingers of a man's hand wrote upon the plaster of the wall over against the candlestick; the king's countenance changed, his thoughts troubled him, the joints of his loins were loosed, and his knees smote one against another
opt3: A winged seraph hovered over the royal table brandishing a sword; the king tore his scarlet garments and wept
opt4: A disembodied voice thundered from heaven while the walls shook; the king's hair turned white and he fled from the room
correct: Fingers of a man's hand wrote upon the plaster of the wall over against the candlestick; the king's countenance changed, his thoughts troubled him, the joints of his loins were loosed, and his knees smote one against another
explanation: Daniel 5:5-6 (KJV) - "In the same hour came forth fingers of a man's hand, and wrote over against the candlestick upon the plaister of the wall of the king's palace: and the king saw the part of the hand that wrote. Then the king's countenance was changed, and his thoughts troubled him, so that the joints of his loins were loosed, and his knees smote one against another."

question: In Daniel 5:7-8, what three royal honors did Belshazzar promise to whoever could read the writing and show its interpretation, and what was the immediate result?
opt1: Given half the kingdom, married to the king's daughter, and made prime minister; yet the astrologers gave conflicting interpretations
opt2: Riding upon the king's horse, crowned with royal diadem, and ruling over Babylon; yet all the Chaldeans were struck dumb
opt3: Clothed with scarlet, a chain of gold about his neck, and be the third ruler in the kingdom; yet none of the king's wise men could read the writing nor make known the interpretation
opt4: Granted exempt status from taxes, showered with silver talents, and made governor of Media; yet the sorcerers fled in fear
correct: Clothed with scarlet, a chain of gold about his neck, and be the third ruler in the kingdom; yet none of the king's wise men could read the writing nor make known the interpretation
explanation: Daniel 5:7-8 (KJV) - "The king cried aloud to bring in the astrologers, the Chaldeans, and the soothsayers. And the king spake, and said to the wise men of Babylon, Whosoever shall read this writing, and shew me the interpretation thereof, shall be clothed with scarlet, and have a chain of gold about his neck, and shall be the third ruler in the kingdom. Then came in all the king's wise men: but they could not read the writing, nor make known to the king the interpretation thereof."

question: According to Daniel 5:10-12, who entered the banquet house to advise the troubled king, and how did she describe the endowments of Daniel?
opt1: The high priestess of Ishtar; she said Daniel possessed ancient Egyptian sorcery and could command the spirits of the underworld
opt2: The daughter of Nebuchadnezzar; she recalled that Daniel had slain a dragon in the days of her father
opt3: The chief eunuch; he testified that Daniel had preserved the royal chronicles during the siege of Jerusalem
opt4: The queen; she stated that in him was the spirit of the holy gods, with light, understanding, wisdom, knowledge, interpreting of dreams, showing of hard sentences, and dissolving of doubts
correct: The queen; she stated that in him was the spirit of the holy gods, with light, understanding, wisdom, knowledge, interpreting of dreams, showing of hard sentences, and dissolving of doubts
explanation: Daniel 5:10-12 (KJV) - "Now the queen, by reason of the words of the king and his lords, came into the banquet house: and the queen spake and said, O king, live for ever: let not thy thoughts trouble thee, nor let thy countenance be changed: There is a man in thy kingdom, in whom is the spirit of the holy gods ... Forasmuch as an excellent spirit, and knowledge, and understanding, interpreting of dreams, and shewing of hard sentences, and dissolving of doubts, were found in the same Daniel, whom the king named Belteshazzar: now let Daniel be called, and he will shew the interpretation."

question: When Belshazzar offered Daniel the scarlet attire, golden chain, and position as third ruler, what was Daniel's disdainful response in Daniel 5:16-17?
opt1: "Let thy gifts be to thyself, and give thy rewards to another; yet I will read the writing unto the king, and make known to him the interpretation"
opt2: "I will accept thy golden chain, but give the scarlet robe to the needy of Babylon"
opt3: "Thy silver and gold shall perish with thee, for thou hast blasphemed the Most High God"
opt4: "I desire neither honor nor rule among uncircumcised idolaters whose end is destruction"
correct: "Let thy gifts be to thyself, and give thy rewards to another; yet I will read the writing unto the king, and make known to him the interpretation"
explanation: Daniel 5:17 (KJV) - "Then Daniel answered and said before the king, Let thy gifts be to thyself, and give thy rewards to another; yet I will read the writing unto the king, and make known to him the interpretation."

question: In Daniel 5:18-21, what historical lesson regarding Nebuchadnezzar's pride did Daniel recount to rebuke Belshazzar?
opt1: Nebuchadnezzar was struck down by the sword of Pharaoh Necho because he refused to pay tribute to the Lord
opt2: When Nebuchadnezzar's heart was lifted up and his mind hardened in pride, he was deposed from his kingly throne, his glory taken, and he was driven from men to dwell with wild asses and eat grass as oxen until he recognized God's rule
opt3: Nebuchadnezzar's firstborn son was slain by a destroying angel because he mocked the golden candlesticks of the temple
opt4: Nebuchadnezzar was blinded by the Assyrians and dragged to Nineveh in chains because he set up a golden idol
correct: When Nebuchadnezzar's heart was lifted up and his mind hardened in pride, he was deposed from his kingly throne, his glory taken, and he was driven from men to dwell with wild asses and eat grass as oxen until he recognized God's rule
explanation: Daniel 5:20-21 (KJV) - "But when his heart was lifted up, and his mind hardened in pride, he was deposed from his kingly throne, and they took his glory from him: And he was driven from the sons of men; and his heart was made like the beasts, and his dwelling was with the wild asses: they fed him with grass like oxen, and his body was wet with the dew of heaven; till he knew that the most high God ruled in the kingdom of men, and that he appointeth over it whomsoever he will."

question: What pointed indictment did Daniel pronounce against Belshazzar in Daniel 5:22-23 before interpreting the inscription?
opt1: Thou hast murdered the prophets of God and shed innocent blood in the streets of Babylon without remorse
opt2: Thou hast neglected the walls of Babylon and squandered the royal treasury on drunken revelries with thy concubines
opt3: Thou his son, O Belshazzar, hast not humbled thine heart, though thou knewest all this; but hast lifted up thyself against the Lord of heaven, and the God in whose hand thy breath is, hast thou not glorified
opt4: Thou hast allied thyself with the pharaoh of Egypt against the decrees of the prophets of Judah
correct: Thou his son, O Belshazzar, hast not humbled thine heart, though thou knewest all this; but hast lifted up thyself against the Lord of heaven, and the God in whose hand thy breath is, hast thou not glorified
explanation: Daniel 5:22-23 (KJV) - "And thou his son, O Belshazzar, hast not humbled thine heart, though thou knewest all this; But hast lifted up thyself against the Lord of heaven; and they have brought the vessels of his house before thee, and thou, and thy lords, thy wives, and thy concubines, have drunk wine in them; and thou hast praised the gods of silver, and gold, of brass, iron, wood, and stone, which see not, nor hear, nor know: and the God in whose hand thy breath is, and whose are all thy ways, hast thou not glorified:"

question: What were the exact words inscribed by the hand upon the plaster of the wall, as revealed in Daniel 5:25?
opt1: "MENE, TEKEL, PERES, BABEL"
opt2: "TEKEL, UPHARSIN, MENE, DARIUS"
opt3: "PERES, MENE, TEKEL, SHINAR"
opt4: "MENE, MENE, TEKEL, UPHARSIN"
correct: "MENE, MENE, TEKEL, UPHARSIN"
explanation: Daniel 5:25 (KJV) - "And this is the writing that was written, MENE, MENE, TEKEL, UPHARSIN."

question: According to Daniel 5:26-28, what is the divine interpretation given by Daniel for MENE, TEKEL, and PERES?
opt1: MENE: God hath numbered thy kingdom, and finished it; TEKEL: Thou art weighed in the balances, and art found wanting; PERES: Thy kingdom is divided, and given to the Medes and Persians
opt2: MENE: Thy days are cut short; TEKEL: Thy gods are powerless; PERES: The Medes shall burn thy palace with fire
opt3: MENE: Thy throne is overturned; TEKEL: Thy sins are multiplied; PERES: Babylon shall become a heap of stones
opt4: MENE: Judgment is decreed; TEKEL: Thy crown is removed; PERES: Cyrus shall possess thy silver and gold
correct: MENE: God hath numbered thy kingdom, and finished it; TEKEL: Thou art weighed in the balances, and art found wanting; PERES: Thy kingdom is divided, and given to the Medes and Persians
explanation: Daniel 5:26-28 (KJV) - "This is the interpretation of the thing: MENE; God hath numbered thy kingdom, and finished it. TEKEL; Thou art weighed in the balances, and art found wanting. PERES; Thy kingdom is divided, and given to the Medes and Persians."

question: In Daniel 5:30-31, what occurred that very night to King Belshazzar, and who seized the kingdom at what age?
opt1: Belshazzar escaped to Borsippa in disguise; and Cyrus the Persian captured Babylon, being forty years old
opt2: Belshazzar the king of the Chaldeans was slain; and Darius the Median took the kingdom, being about threescore and two years old
opt3: Belshazzar was poisoned by his own cupbearer; and Astyages the Mede assumed the crown, being seventy years old
opt4: Belshazzar surrendered to the Persian army at dawn; and Cambyses took the throne, being thirty-five years old
correct: Belshazzar the king of the Chaldeans was slain; and Darius the Median took the kingdom, being about threescore and two years old
explanation: Daniel 5:30-31 (KJV) - "In that night was Belshazzar the king of the Chaldeans slain. And Darius the Median took the kingdom, being about threescore and two years old."

question: In Daniel 6:1-3, how many princes did Darius appoint over the realm, how many presidents were set over them, and why was Daniel preferred above all?
opt1: 70 princes; 7 presidents, of whom Daniel was the youngest; because he interpreted the king's royal dreams
opt2: 120 princes; 3 presidents, of whom Daniel was first; because an excellent spirit was in him, and the king thought to set him over the whole realm
opt3: 100 princes; 4 presidents, of whom Daniel was treasurer; because he had preserved the Persian archives
opt4: 127 princes; 2 presidents, of whom Daniel was scribe; because he was loved by the Median army commanders
correct: 120 princes; 3 presidents, of whom Daniel was first; because an excellent spirit was in him, and the king thought to set him over the whole realm
explanation: Daniel 6:1-3 (KJV) - "It pleased Darius to set over the kingdom an hundred and twenty princes, which should be over the whole kingdom; And over these three presidents; of whom Daniel was first: that the princes might give accounts unto them, and the king should have no damage. Then this Daniel was preferred above the presidents and princes, because an excellent spirit was in him; and the king thought to set him over the whole realm."

question: According to Daniel 6:4-5, when the jealous presidents and princes sought occasion against Daniel concerning the kingdom, what conclusion did they reach?
opt1: They discovered that he had secretly remitted taxes for Judahite exiles, yet dared not accuse him openly
opt2: They found that he had refused to bow before the royal standard, but had the protection of Darius
opt3: They could find none occasion nor fault, forasmuch as he was faithful, neither was there any error or fault found in him; concluding they could find occasion only concerning the law of his God
opt4: They could find no financial corruption, but planned to bribe false witnesses to testify that he practiced treason
correct: They could find none occasion nor fault, forasmuch as he was faithful, neither was there any error or fault found in him; concluding they could find occasion only concerning the law of his God
explanation: Daniel 6:4-5 (KJV) - "Then the presidents and princes sought to find occasion against Daniel concerning the kingdom; but they could find none occasion nor fault; forasmuch as he was faithful, neither was there any error or fault found in him. Then said these men, We shall not find any occasion against this Daniel, except we find it against him concerning the law of his God."

question: In Daniel 6:6-9, what royal statute did the conspirators flatter Darius into signing, which according to the law of the Medes and Persians could not be altered?
opt1: Whosoever shall fail to bow before the golden image of Darius at the rising of the sun shall be burned alive
opt2: Whosoever shall keep any Hebrew religious scroll in his household for forty days shall forfeit all his property
opt3: Whosoever shall sacrifice to any deity other than Ahura Mazda for three months shall be banished from the empire
opt4: Whosoever shall ask a petition of any God or man for thirty days, save of the king, shall be cast into the den of lions
correct: Whosoever shall ask a petition of any God or man for thirty days, save of the king, shall be cast into the den of lions
explanation: Daniel 6:7-8 (KJV) - "All the presidents of the kingdom, the governors, and the princes, the counsellors, and the captains, have consulted together to establish a royal statute, and to make a firm decree, that whosoever shall ask a petition of any God or man for thirty days, save of thee, O king, he shall be cast into the den of lions. Now, O king, establish the decree, and sign the writing, that it be not changed, according to the law of the Medes and Persians, which altereth not."

question: What did Daniel do when he knew that the royal writing was signed, as described in Daniel 6:10?
opt1: He went into his house, his windows being open in his chamber toward Jerusalem, he kneeled upon his knees three times a day, and prayed, and gave thanks before his God, as he did aforetime
opt2: He closed his windows and prayed in absolute silence at midnight so that no conspirator could overhear him
opt3: He fled to the temple of Bel to claim sanctuary under the ancient laws of Babylonian kings
opt4: He drafted an urgent petition to Darius demanding that the royal decree be revoked as unconstitutional
correct: He went into his house, his windows being open in his chamber toward Jerusalem, he kneeled upon his knees three times a day, and prayed, and gave thanks before his God, as he did aforetime
explanation: Daniel 6:10 (KJV) - "Now when Daniel knew that the writing was signed, he went into his house; and his windows being open in his chamber toward Jerusalem, he kneeled upon his knees three times a day, and prayed, and gave thanks before his God, as he did aforetime."

question: In Daniel 6:14-16, how did King Darius react upon hearing the accusation against Daniel, and what parting words did he speak as Daniel was cast into the lions' den?
opt1: He flew into a rage against the conspirators, offering them half his treasury; and said, "May Cyrus avenge thee!"
opt2: He was sore displeased with himself, set his heart on Daniel to deliver him till sunset; and said to Daniel, "Thy God whom thou servest continually, he will deliver thee"
opt3: He wept openly before his satraps, refusing to eat; and said to Daniel, "If there be any justice in heaven, thou shalt live!"
opt4: He attempted to pardon Daniel by royal prerogative; and whispered, "Trust in the archangels of Judah!"
correct: He was sore displeased with himself, set his heart on Daniel to deliver him till sunset; and said to Daniel, "Thy God whom thou servest continually, he will deliver thee"
explanation: Daniel 6:14, 16 (KJV) - "Then the king, when he heard these words, was sore displeased with himself, and set his heart on Daniel to deliver him: and he laboured till the going down of the sun to deliver him ... Then the king commanded, and they brought Daniel, and cast him into the den of lions. Now the king spake and said unto Daniel, Thy God whom thou servest continually, he will deliver thee."

question: According to Daniel 6:17-18, how was the entrance of the den secured, and how did Darius spend that night in his palace?
opt1: An iron gate was locked with seven royal chains; the king drank heavily until dawn to drown his grief
opt2: A bronze door was sealed with molten lead; the king consulted his sorcerers all night to break the curse
opt3: A stone was laid upon the mouth of the den, sealed with the king's signet and that of his lords; the king spent the night fasting, no instruments of musick were brought, and his sleep went from him
opt4: Heavy boulders were rolled against the mouth and guarded by 100 soldiers; the king walked the battlements in sackcloth
correct: A stone was laid upon the mouth of the den, sealed with the king's signet and that of his lords; the king spent the night fasting, no instruments of musick were brought, and his sleep went from him
explanation: Daniel 6:17-18 (KJV) - "And a stone was brought, and laid upon the mouth of the den; and the king sealed it with his own signet, and with the signet of his lords; that the purpose might not be changed concerning Daniel. Then the king went to his palace, and passed the night fasting: neither were instruments of musick brought before him: and his sleep went from him."

question: In Daniel 6:19-22, when Darius went in haste to the den very early in the morning and cried with a lamentable voice, what testimony of deliverance did Daniel give?
opt1: "The Lord of hosts sent a slumber upon the lions, and I rested upon their manes throughout the night in peace"
opt2: "An invisible wall of heavenly fire surrounded me, and the beasts dared not approach within ten cubits"
opt3: "The angel Michael stood beside me with a drawn sword, and the beasts trembled at the presence of the Lord"
opt4: "My God hath sent his angel, and hath shut the lions' mouths, that they have not hurt me: forasmuch as before him innocency was found in me; and also before thee, O king, have I done no hurt"

question: In Daniel 8:1-4, in which year of Belshazzar was this vision seen, where was Daniel located, and how is the two-horned ram described?

question: According to Daniel 8:5-7, what creature approached from the west on the face of the whole earth without touching the ground, and what violence did he inflict upon the ram?

question: According to Daniel 8:15-16, who had the appearance of a man standing before Daniel, and who was commanded by a voice from between the banks of Ulai to make him understand?
