question: According to Daniel 9:3-5, with what spiritual disciplines and opening corporate confession did Daniel set his face unto the Lord God?
opt1: By offering bullocks and rams upon an altar of unhewn stone; proclaiming, "Israel is pure, but Babylon hath oppressed us unjustly"
opt2: By prayer and supplications, with fasting, and sackcloth, and ashes; confessing, "We have sinned, and have committed iniquity, and have done wickedly, and have rebelled, even by departing from thy precepts and from thy judgments"
opt3: By washing seven times in the river Tigris; petitioning, "Remember the righteousness of Abraham and overlook the idolatry of our fathers"
opt4: By blowing the silver jubilee trumpets at sunset; praying, "Avenge thy holy sanctuary upon the uncircumcised nations of Shinar"
correct: By prayer and supplications, with fasting, and sackcloth, and ashes; confessing, "We have sinned, and have committed iniquity, and have done wickedly, and have rebelled, even by departing from thy precepts and from thy judgments"
explanation: Daniel 9:3, 5 (KJV) - "And I set my face unto the Lord God, to seek by prayer and supplications, with fasting, and sackcloth, and ashes: And I prayed unto the LORD my God, and made my confession, and said ... We have sinned, and have committed iniquity, and have done wickedly, and have rebelled, even by departing from thy precepts and from thy judgments:"

question: In Daniel 9:7-9, how does Daniel contrast the moral character of the Lord with that of Judah, their kings, princes, and fathers?
opt1: Unto the Lord belongeth unbending vengeance, but unto us mourning and lamentation, because no forgiveness can be found
opt2: Unto the Lord belongeth sovereign silence, but unto us continuous supplication until He remembereth Mount Zion
opt3: Unto the Lord belongeth righteousness, but unto us confusion of faces; yet unto the Lord our God belong mercies and forgivenesses, though we have rebelled against Him
opt4: Unto the Lord belongeth the temple of gold, but unto us exile in mud-brick huts until seventy jubilees are accomplished
correct: Unto the Lord belongeth righteousness, but unto us confusion of faces; yet unto the Lord our God belong mercies and forgivenesses, though we have rebelled against Him
explanation: Daniel 9:7-9 (KJV) - "O Lord, righteousness belongeth unto thee, but unto us confusion of faces, as at this day; to the men of Judah, and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and unto all Israel, that are near, and that are far off ... To the Lord our God belong mercies and forgivenesses, though we have rebelled against him;"

question: According to Daniel 9:11-14, what ancient covenant consequence was poured out upon Israel, and why did the Lord watch upon the evil to bring it upon them?
opt1: The plague of the Philistines; for the Lord had forgotten His covenant because of Manasseh's shedding of innocent blood
opt2: The captivity of Egypt renewed; for the angels of judgment demanded immediate satisfaction against the house of David
opt3: The desolation of Sodom; for the Lord would no longer endure their Sabbath violations and foreign idolatries
opt4: The curse and oath written in the law of Moses the servant of God; for the Lord our God is righteous in all His works which He doeth, and they obeyed not His voice
correct: The curse and oath written in the law of Moses the servant of God; for the Lord our God is righteous in all His works which He doeth, and they obeyed not His voice
explanation: Daniel 9:11, 14 (KJV) - "Yea, all Israel have transgressed thy law, even by departing, that they might not obey thy voice; therefore the curse is poured upon us, and the oath that is written in the law of Moses the servant of God, because we have sinned against him ... Therefore hath the LORD watched upon the evil, and brought it upon us: for the LORD our God is righteous in all his works which he doeth: for we obeyed not his voice."

question: In Daniel 9:17-19, on what sole basis does Daniel plead for God to hear his prayer, cause His face to shine upon His sanctuary, and defer not?
opt1: "We do not present our supplications before thee for our righteousnesses, but for thy great mercies ... O Lord, hear; O Lord, forgive; O Lord, hearken and do; defer not, for thine own sake, O my God: for thy city and thy people are called by thy name"
opt2: "We plead the ancient merit of David our king, who purchased the threshingfloor of Araunah with silver shekels"
opt3: "We bring before thee the tears of our weeping children and the ashes of the burnt cedar beams of thy temple"
opt4: "We vow to keep all the statutes of the Levitical priesthood without fault for ten generations if thou wilt deliver us"
correct: "We do not present our supplications before thee for our righteousnesses, but for thy great mercies ... O Lord, hear; O Lord, forgive; O Lord, hearken and do; defer not, for thine own sake, O my God: for thy city and thy people are called by thy name"
explanation: Daniel 9:18-19 (KJV) - "O my God, incline thine ear, and hear; open thine eyes, and behold our desolations, and the city which is called by thy name: for we do not present our supplications before thee for our righteousnesses, but for thy great mercies. O Lord, hear; O Lord, forgive; O Lord, hearken and do; defer not, for thine own sake, O my God: for thy city and thy people are called by thy name."

question: According to Daniel 9:20-21, who arrived while Daniel was speaking, praying, and confessing his sin, and at what specific time of day did he touch him?
opt1: The archangel Michael, descending with a drawn sword, touched his shoulder at the third hour of the morning sacrifice
opt2: The man Gabriel, whom he had seen in the vision at the beginning, being caused to fly swiftly, touched him about the time of the evening oblation
opt3: A celestial seraph, bearing a live coal from the altar, touched his lips at the exact moment the sun set over Babylon
opt4: The prophet Jeremiah in a glorious vision, holding a golden inkhorn, appeared at the stroke of midnight
correct: The man Gabriel, whom he had seen in the vision at the beginning, being caused to fly swiftly, touched him about the time of the evening oblation
explanation: Daniel 9:21 (KJV) - "Yea, whiles I was speaking in prayer, even the man Gabriel, whom I had seen in the vision at the beginning, being caused to fly swiftly, touched me about the time of the evening oblation."

question: What loving designation did Gabriel apply to Daniel in Daniel 9:22-23 to explain why the divine commandment came forth at the beginning of his supplications?
opt1: For thou art a righteous prince in Israel: whose prayers have surpassed the intercession of Moses
opt2: For thou art the faithful watchman of Judah: appointed to unlock the hidden gates of prophecy
opt3: For thou art greatly beloved: therefore understand the matter, and consider the vision
opt4: For thy fasting hath moved the throne of heaven: and thy tears are preserved in golden vials
correct: For thou art greatly beloved: therefore understand the matter, and consider the vision
explanation: Daniel 9:23 (KJV) - "At the beginning of thy supplications the commandment came forth, and I am come to shew thee; for thou art greatly beloved: therefore understand the matter, and consider the vision."

question: In Daniel 9:24, what six prophetic objectives are decreed to be accomplished upon Daniel's people and the holy city within the span of seventy weeks?
opt1: To rebuild the temple walls, to crown a son of Zerubbabel, to vanquish the Samaritans, to restore the ark, to cleanse the Levites, and to burn the idols of Shinar
opt2: To conquer the Persian empire, to restore the twelve tribal allotments, to gather the diaspora, to erect the bronze altar, to establish jubilee, and to sanctify Mount Zion
opt3: To punish the Chaldeans, to open the gates of Jerusalem, to translate the Law into Greek, to build seventy synagogues, to defeat Antiochus, and to purify the priesthood
opt4: To finish the transgression, to make an end of sins, to make reconciliation for iniquity, to bring in everlasting righteousness, to seal up the vision and prophecy, and to anoint the most Holy
correct: To finish the transgression, to make an end of sins, to make reconciliation for iniquity, to bring in everlasting righteousness, to seal up the vision and prophecy, and to anoint the most Holy
explanation: Daniel 9:24 (KJV) - "Seventy weeks are determined upon thy people and upon thy holy city, to finish the transgression, and to make an end of sins, and to make reconciliation for iniquity, and to bring in everlasting righteousness, and to seal up the vision and prophecy, and to anoint the most Holy."

question: According to Daniel 9:25-26, how are the weeks partitioned from the decree to restore Jerusalem unto Messiah the Prince, and what shall occur after threescore and two weeks?
opt1: Seven weeks, and threescore and two weeks; and after threescore and two weeks shall Messiah be cut off, but not for himself: and the people of the prince that shall come shall destroy the city and the sanctuary
opt2: Three weeks, and forty weeks; after which Messiah shall conquer the nations with an iron rod and rebuild the palace of Solomon
opt3: Ten weeks, and fifty weeks; after which Messiah shall be crowned king in Shushan and lead the exiles back in triumph
opt4: Twelve weeks, and sixty weeks; after which Messiah shall seal the books of prophecy and abolish all Gentile kingdoms
correct: Seven weeks, and threescore and two weeks; and after threescore and two weeks shall Messiah be cut off, but not for himself: and the people of the prince that shall come shall destroy the city and the sanctuary
explanation: Daniel 9:25-26 (KJV) - "Know therefore and understand, that from the going forth of the commandment to restore and to build Jerusalem unto the Messiah the Prince shall be seven weeks, and threescore and two weeks: the street shall be built again, and the wall, even in troublous times. And after threescore and two weeks shall Messiah be cut off, but not for himself: and the people of the prince that shall come shall destroy the city and the sanctuary; and the end thereof shall be with a flood, and unto the end of the war desolations are determined."

question: In Daniel 9:27, what covenant events and desolations are prophesied to occur in the final (seventieth) week?
opt1: He shall restore the daily burnt offering for one full week; in the midst of which all nations shall gather to worship at the bronze altar in peace
opt2: He shall confirm the covenant with many for one week; in the midst of the week he shall cause the sacrifice and the oblation to cease, and for the overspreading of abominations he shall make it desolate, even until the consummation
opt3: He shall break the Persian yoke for seven months; after which the temple treasury shall be filled with golden vessels from Babylon
opt4: He shall establish a seven-year truce with the kings of the south; after which the city of Jerusalem shall be burned by fire from heaven
correct: He shall confirm the covenant with many for one week; in the midst of the week he shall cause the sacrifice and the oblation to cease, and for the overspreading of abominations he shall make it desolate, even until the consummation
explanation: Daniel 9:27 (KJV) - "And he shall confirm the covenant with many for one week: and in the midst of the week he shall cause the sacrifice and the oblation to cease, and for the overspreading of abominations he shall make it desolate, even until the consummation, and that determined shall be poured upon the desolate."

question: In Daniel 10:1-3, in the third year of Cyrus king of Persia, what was Daniel's manner of mourning, and for what exact period of time did he observe it?
opt1: He fasted forty literal days and forty nights: drinking only bitter water and sleeping upon bare rock outside the city of Susa
opt2: He mourned three full weeks: ate no pleasant bread, neither came flesh nor wine in his mouth, nor did he anoint himself at all, till three whole weeks were fulfilled
opt3: He sat in sackcloth for seven days: abstaining from all food and water while interceding for the return of the exiles
opt4: He wept for seventy days: refusing royal delicacies and pouring dust upon his head every morning by the river Euphrates
correct: He mourned three full weeks: ate no pleasant bread, neither came flesh nor wine in his mouth, nor did he anoint himself at all, till three whole weeks were fulfilled
explanation: Daniel 10:2-3 (KJV) - "In those days I Daniel was mourning three full weeks. I ate no pleasant bread, neither came flesh nor wine in my mouth, neither did I anoint myself at all, till three whole weeks were fulfilled."

question: According to Daniel 10:4-6, by the side of what great river was Daniel on the four and twentieth day of the first month, and how is the glorious heavenly man described?
opt1: By the river Chebar; arrayed in white wool, holding a measuring reed, face shining like the midday sun, feet like burning coals
opt2: By the river of Ulai; crowned with a golden diadem, riding upon a white stallion, holding seven thunderbolts in his right hand
opt3: By the side of the great river Hiddekel; clothed in linen, loins girded with fine gold of Uphaz, body like beryl, face as lightning, eyes as lamps of fire, arms and feet like polished brass, voice like the voice of a multitude
opt4: By the brook Kidron; girded with a sash of scarlet, holding an inkhorn of ivory, voice like a rushing waterfall
correct: By the side of the great river Hiddekel; clothed in linen, loins girded with fine gold of Uphaz, body like beryl, face as lightning, eyes as lamps of fire, arms and feet like polished brass, voice like the voice of a multitude
explanation: Daniel 10:4-6 (KJV) - "And in the four and twentieth day of the first month, as I was by the side of the great river, which is Hiddekel; Then I lifted up mine eyes, and looked, and behold a certain man clothed in linen, whose loins were girded with fine gold of Uphaz: His body also was like the beryl, and his face as the appearance of lightning, and his eyes as lamps of fire, and his arms and his feet like in colour to polished brass, and the voice of his words like the voice of a multitude."

question: In Daniel 10:7-9, what reaction did the men with Daniel have when the vision appeared, and what physical effect overcame Daniel?
opt1: The men were struck blind and cried out in agony; Daniel stood erect and conversed with the messenger for three hours in Aramaic
opt2: The men fell prostrate and worshiped the heavenly appearance; Daniel was transported bodily into the third heaven above the stars
opt3: The men drew their swords thinking an enemy had invaded; Daniel was enveloped in a pillar of cloud and vanished from their sight
opt4: The men saw not the vision, but a great quaking fell upon them so that they fled to hide; Daniel was left alone, his comeliness turned into corruption, he retained no strength, and fell into a deep sleep on his face toward the ground
correct: The men saw not the vision, but a great quaking fell upon them so that they fled to hide; Daniel was left alone, his comeliness turned into corruption, he retained no strength, and fell into a deep sleep on his face toward the ground
explanation: Daniel 10:7-9 (KJV) - "And I Daniel alone saw the vision: for the men that were with me saw not the vision; but a great quaking fell upon them, so that they fled to hide themselves. Therefore I was left alone, and saw this great vision, and there remained no strength in me: for my comeliness was turned in me into corruption, and I retained no strength. Yet heard I the voice of his words: and when I heard the voice of his words, then was I in a deep sleep on my face, and my face toward the ground."

question: According to Daniel 10:10-12, when a hand touched Daniel and set him upon his knees and palms, what comfort did the messenger speak regarding when his prayer was heard?
opt1: "Fear not, Daniel: for from the first day that thou didst set thine heart to understand, and to chasten thyself before thy God, thy words were heard, and I am come for thy words"
opt2: "Weep no more, Daniel: for after twenty-one days of fasting thy penance has finally satisfied the justice of the Almighty"
opt3: "Arise, son of Judah: for the decree of Cyrus has been signed and thy people are already marching toward Mount Zion"
opt4: "Stand upon thy feet: for the Lord hath dispatched me only after all the princes of Media bowed before His altar"
correct: "Fear not, Daniel: for from the first day that thou didst set thine heart to understand, and to chasten thyself before thy God, thy words were heard, and I am come for thy words"
explanation: Daniel 10:11-12 (KJV) - "And he said unto me, O Daniel, a man greatly beloved, understand the words that I speak unto thee, and stand upright: for unto thee am I now sent. And when he had spoken this word unto me, I stood trembling. Then said he unto me, Fear not, Daniel: for from the first day that thou didst set thine heart to understand, and to chasten thyself before thy God, thy words were heard, and I am come for thy words."

question: In Daniel 10:13, what cosmic spiritual conflict delayed the celestial messenger for twenty-one days, and who came to his assistance?
opt1: The dragon of the Euphrates blocked his path across the mountains; but Gabriel summoned twelve legions of angels to clear the way
opt2: The prince of the kingdom of Persia withstood him one and twenty days; but Michael, one of the chief princes, came to help him
opt3: The spirit of Babylon held the golden gates of heaven shut; but the angel of the covenant smote the lock with a rod of iron
opt4: The prince of Grecia contested the sovereignty over the satrapies; but Uriel brought a scroll containing the divine decree
correct: The prince of the kingdom of Persia withstood him one and twenty days; but Michael, one of the chief princes, came to help him
explanation: Daniel 10:13 (KJV) - "But the prince of the kingdom of Persia withstood me one and twenty days: but, lo, Michael, one of the chief princes, came to help me; and I remained there with the kings of Persia."

question: According to Daniel 10:14, what is the stated purpose and chronological horizon of the revelation the messenger was sent to impart?
opt1: "I am come to reveal the exact date when the foundations of the second temple shall be laid by Zerubbabel"
opt2: "I am sent to recount the history of the kings of Judah from Rehoboam unto the Babylonian captivity"
opt3: "Now I am come to make thee understand what shall befall thy people in the latter days: for yet the vision is for many days"
opt4: "I am come to warn thee concerning the secret poison prepared against King Cyrus by the magicians of Chaldea"
correct: "Now I am come to make thee understand what shall befall thy people in the latter days: for yet the vision is for many days"
explanation: Daniel 10:14 (KJV) - "Now I am come to make thee understand what shall befall thy people in the latter days: for yet the vision is for many days."

question: In Daniel 10:15-17, when Daniel set his face toward the ground and was struck dumb, how was his speech restored, and what physical helplessness did he confess?
opt1: An angel touched his tongue with honey from heaven; Daniel proclaimed that his mind was clear, though his legs were paralyzed
opt2: A voice commanded him to breathe the breath of life; Daniel stated that his eyes were blinded by the radiance of the gold of Uphaz
opt3: A celestial coal touched his mouth; Daniel declared that his heart was leaping within him like a hunted gazelle
opt4: One like the similitude of the sons of men touched his lips; Daniel confessed that his sorrows were turned upon him, no strength remained in him, neither was there breath left in him
correct: One like the similitude of the sons of men touched his lips; Daniel confessed that his sorrows were turned upon him, no strength remained in him, neither was there breath left in him
explanation: Daniel 10:16-17 (KJV) - "And, behold, one like the similitude of the sons of men touched my lips: then I opened my mouth, and spake, and said unto him that stood before me, O my lord, by the vision my sorrows are turned upon me, and I have retained no strength. For how can the servant of this my lord talk with this my lord? for as for me, straightway there remained no strength in me, neither is there breath left in me."

question: According to Daniel 10:18-19, who touched Daniel a second time to strengthen him, and with what encouraging benediction?
opt1: There came again and touched him one like the appearance of a man, and he strengthened him, and said, "O man greatly beloved, fear not: peace be unto thee, be strong, yea, be strong"
opt2: The archangel Gabriel touched him with a silver sceptre, saying, "Blessed art thou among all the prophets of Judah: fear neither beast nor king"
opt3: Michael the great prince grasped his right hand, declaring, "The victory is won in the heavenlies: stand forth as a mighty warrior"
opt4: A seraph clothed in flame embraced him, saying, "Grace and glory be multiplied unto thee: the kingdom of thy God shall endure forever"
correct: There came again and touched him one like the appearance of a man, and he strengthened him, and said, "O man greatly beloved, fear not: peace be unto thee, be strong, yea, be strong"
explanation: Daniel 10:18-19 (KJV) - "Then there came again and touched me one like the appearance of a man, and he strengthened me, And said, O man greatly beloved, fear not: peace be unto thee, be strong, yea, be strong. And when he had spoken unto me, I was strengthened, and said, Let my lord speak; for thou hast strengthened me."

question: In Daniel 10:20, against which two territorial spiritual powers did the messenger declare he must wage battle after departing from Daniel?
opt1: He must contend with the prince of Babylon and the prince of Egypt
opt2: He must return to fight with the prince of Persia; and when he is gone forth, lo, the prince of Grecia shall come
opt3: He must overthrow the prince of Rome and the prince of Assyria
opt4: He must subdue the prince of Tyre and the prince of Edom
correct: He must return to fight with the prince of Persia; and when he is gone forth, lo, the prince of Grecia shall come
explanation: Daniel 10:20 (KJV) - "Then said he, Knowest thou wherefore I come unto thee? and now will I return to fight with the prince of Persia: and when I am gone forth, lo, the prince of Grecia shall come."

question: What title does the heavenly messenger give to the prophetic writing he will show, and who alone stands with him in these spiritual warfare matters in Daniel 10:21?
opt1: "The book of the wars of the Lord"; and none stood with him except Gabriel the interpreter
opt2: "The royal chronicles of heaven"; and none held with him except the seven spirits before the throne
opt3: "The scripture of truth"; and there is none that holdeth with him in these things, but Michael your prince
opt4: "The covenant of the latter days"; and none supported him except the guardian angel of Jerusalem
correct: "The scripture of truth"; and there is none that holdeth with him in these things, but Michael your prince
explanation: Daniel 10:21 (KJV) - "But I will shew thee that which is noted in the scripture of truth: and there is none that holdeth with me in these things, but Michael your prince."

question: In Daniel 11:1-2, how many kings were prophesied yet to stand up in Persia, and what is foretold concerning the wealth and ambition of the fourth king?
opt1: Seven kings shall rule in Persia; and the fourth shall conquer Egypt and Ethiopia, building a golden palace in Babylon
opt2: Four kings shall arise in Susa; and the fourth shall convert to the worship of the God of Judah and rebuild the temple walls
opt3: Three kings shall stand up yet in Persia; and the fourth shall be far richer than they all, and by his strength through his riches he shall stir up all against the realm of Grecia
opt4: Two kings shall reign in Media; and the fourth shall be overthrown by an insurrection of his own satraps
correct: Three kings shall stand up yet in Persia; and the fourth shall be far richer than they all, and by his strength through his riches he shall stir up all against the realm of Grecia
explanation: Daniel 11:2 (KJV) - "And now will I shew thee the truth. Behold, there shall stand up yet three kings in Persia; and the fourth shall be far richer than they all: and by his strength through his riches he shall stir up all against the realm of Grecia."

question: According to Daniel 11:3-4, what mighty king shall stand up, and what shall happen to his empire upon his demise?
opt1: A king of fierce countenance shall conquer the known world; and his kingdom shall be inherited by his twin sons in unbroken succession
opt2: A wise philosopher-king shall establish universal peace; but his empire shall dissolve into twenty autonomous city-states
opt3: A conqueror from the north shall subdue all Asia; but his kingdom shall be consumed by an earthquake within ten months
opt4: A mighty king shall stand up, that shall rule with great dominion, and do according to his will; but his kingdom shall be broken, and divided toward the four winds of heaven, not to his posterity, nor according to his dominion
correct: A mighty king shall stand up, that shall rule with great dominion, and do according to his will; but his kingdom shall be broken, and divided toward the four winds of heaven, not to his posterity, nor according to his dominion
explanation: Daniel 11:3-4 (KJV) - "And a mighty king shall stand up, that shall rule with great dominion, and do according to his will. And when he shall stand up, his kingdom shall be broken, and shall be divided toward the four winds of heaven; and not to his posterity, nor according to his dominion which he ruled: for his kingdom shall be plucked up, even for others beside those."

question: In Daniel 11:5-6, what political alliance is attempted between the king of the south and the king of the north, and what will be its tragic outcome?
opt1: The king's daughter of the south shall come to the king of the north to make an agreement; but she shall not retain the power of the arm, neither shall he stand, but she shall be given up with them that brought her
opt2: The two monarchs shall sign a treaty of trade at Damascus; but the northern king will betray the covenant and poison the southern ambassador
opt3: A joint military expedition against Rome shall be launched; but the southern navy will suffer shipwreck off the coast of Cyprus
opt4: The high priest of Jerusalem will mediate a peace pact; but the northern army will violate the Sabbath and sack the southern capital
correct: The king's daughter of the south shall come to the king of the north to make an agreement; but she shall not retain the power of the arm, neither shall he stand, but she shall be given up with them that brought her
explanation: Daniel 11:6 (KJV) - "And in the end of years they shall join themselves together; for the king's daughter of the south shall come to the king of the north to make an agreement: but she shall not retain the power of the arm; neither shall he stand, nor his arm: but she shall be given up, and they that brought her, and he that begat her, and he that strengthened her in these times."

question: According to Daniel 11:7-9, what shall a branch of her roots accomplish against the fortress of the king of the north?
opt1: He shall burn Antioch to the ground, slaughter sixty thousand northern troops, and annex Syria to the kingdom of the Ptolemies
opt2: He shall enter into the fortress of the king of the north, deal against them, prevail, and carry captive into Egypt their gods with their molten images and precious vessels of silver and of gold
opt3: He shall besiege Babylon for three years, starve the garrison, and carry away the golden image of Dura into Alexandria
opt4: He shall lay tribute upon all the coastal cities of Phoenicia and execute the royal prince of the Seleucid house
correct: He shall enter into the fortress of the king of the north, deal against them, prevail, and carry captive into Egypt their gods with their molten images and precious vessels of silver and of gold
explanation: Daniel 11:7-8 (KJV) - "But out of a branch of her roots shall one stand up in his estate, which shall come with an army, and shall enter into the fortress of the king of the north, and shall deal against them, and shall prevail: And shall also carry captives into Egypt their gods, with their princes, and with their precious vessels of silver and of gold; and he shall continue more years than the king of the north."

question: In Daniel 11:10-15, how does the military conflict escalate between the king of the south and the king of the north?
opt1: The king of the north deploys war elephants to crush the southern cavalry; but a plague decimates both armies on the plains of Megiddo
opt2: The king of the south establishes an alliance with Carthage; but the northern monarch bribes the mercenaries to mutiny
opt3: The king of the south, moved with choler, goes forth to fight and defeats a great multitude; yet his heart is lifted up and he does not strengthen himself, and the king of the north returns with a far greater multitude and equipment, casting up a mount to take the most fenced cities
opt4: Both kings engage in a single combat between champions at Pelusium; resulting in a draw and forty years of guerrilla border skirmishes
correct: The king of the south, moved with choler, goes forth to fight and defeats a great multitude; yet his heart is lifted up and he does not strengthen himself, and the king of the north returns with a far greater multitude and equipment, casting up a mount to take the most fenced cities
explanation: Daniel 11:11, 13, 15 (KJV) - "And the king of the south shall be moved with choler, and shall come forth and fight with him, even with the king of the north: and he shall set forth a great multitude; but the multitude shall be given into his hand ... For the king of the north shall return, and shall set forth a multitude greater than the former ... So the king of the north shall come, and cast up a mount, and take the most fenced cities: and the arms of the south shall not withstand, neither his chosen people, neither shall there be any strength to withstand."

question: According to Daniel 11:21-22, how shall the vile person (Antiochus IV Epiphanes) obtain the kingdom of the north, and who shall be broken before him?
opt1: He shall conquer Antioch through a bloody coup, slaying the rightful heir in the senate; and the high priest of Onias shall crown him
opt2: He shall purchase the crown from the Roman senate with twenty thousand gold talents; and the governor of Samaria shall be executed
opt3: He shall marry the widow of Seleucus IV and poison her sons; and the king of Egypt shall be shattered in open battle
opt4: He shall come in peaceably, and obtain the kingdom by flatteries; and with the arms of a flood shall they be overflown from before him, and shall be broken; yea, also the prince of the covenant
correct: He shall come in peaceably, and obtain the kingdom by flatteries; and with the arms of a flood shall they be overflown from before him, and shall be broken; yea, also the prince of the covenant
explanation: Daniel 11:21-22 (KJV) - "And in his estate shall stand up a vile person, to whom they shall not give the honour of the kingdom: but he shall come in peaceably, and obtain the kingdom by flatteries. And with the arms of a flood shall they be overflown from before him, and shall be broken; yea, also the prince of the covenant."

question: In Daniel 11:28-30, when returning from his expedition toward the south, what naval intervention frustrates the vile person, and against what does he unleash his wrath?
opt1: The ships of Chittim shall come against him, therefore he shall be grieved, and return, and have indignation against the holy covenant: so shall he do; he shall even return, and have intelligence with them that forsake the holy covenant
opt2: The pirate fleets of Cilicia shall blockade his supply lines, causing him to burn the city of Tyre in reckless rage
opt3: The triremes of Alexandria shall sink his flagship off Pelusium, driving him to plunder the temple of Apollo in Greece
opt4: A Roman legion shall besiege his camp at Memphis, forcing him to pay an indemnity of gold and execute his chief general
correct: The ships of Chittim shall come against him, therefore he shall be grieved, and return, and have indignation against the holy covenant: so shall he do; he shall even return, and have intelligence with them that forsake the holy covenant
explanation: Daniel 11:30 (KJV) - "For the ships of Chittim shall come against him: therefore he shall be grieved, and return, and have indignation against the holy covenant: so shall he do; he shall even return, and have intelligence with them that forsake the holy covenant."

question: According to Daniel 11:31-32, what desecrations shall his armed forces execute in the temple, and what contrast is drawn between apostates and the faithful?
opt1: They will melt down the golden table of shewbread and execute seven hundred Levites; the cowards will flee to Pella, but the priests will fast forty days
opt2: Arms shall stand on his part, pollute the sanctuary of strength, take away the daily sacrifice, and place the abomination that maketh desolate; covenant-breakers will be corrupted by flatteries, but the people that do know their God shall be strong, and do exploits
opt3: They will erect an altar to Baal-zebub in the outer court and burn the scrolls of Isaiah; many will convert to paganism, but the Nazarites will slay the garrison
opt4: They will convert the temple into a fortress for Syrian mercenaries; all Judah will bow to Zeus, while only Daniel's disciples remain faithful in secret
correct: Arms shall stand on his part, pollute the sanctuary of strength, take away the daily sacrifice, and place the abomination that maketh desolate; covenant-breakers will be corrupted by flatteries, but the people that do know their God shall be strong, and do exploits
explanation: Daniel 11:31-32 (KJV) - "And arms shall stand on his part, and they shall pollute the sanctuary of strength, and shall take away the daily sacrifice, and they shall place the abomination that maketh desolate. And such as do wickedly against the covenant shall he corrupt by flatteries: but the people that do know their God shall be strong, and do exploits."

question: In Daniel 11:36-38, how is the willful king described in his ultimate blasphemous self-deification, and what strange deity will he honor?
opt1: He shall declare himself the reincarnation of Apollo, commanding universal animal sacrifices; honoring the queen of heaven with incense and cakes
opt2: He shall build a temple to the unknown god of Babylon, rejecting all ancestral deities; spending the royal treasury on colossal brass statues
opt3: He shall do according to his will, exalt and magnify himself above every god, speaking marvellous things against the God of gods; regarding neither the God of his fathers nor the desire of women, but honoring the God of forces with gold, silver, precious stones, and pleasant things
opt4: He shall worship the sun at dawn upon the pinnacle of the temple, forbidding prayer to any other power; honoring the goddess Fortuna with human blood
correct: He shall do according to his will, exalt and magnify himself above every god, speaking marvellous things against the God of gods; regarding neither the God of his fathers nor the desire of women, but honoring the God of forces with gold, silver, precious stones, and pleasant things
explanation: Daniel 11:36-38 (KJV) - "And the king shall do according to his will; and he shall exalt himself, and magnify himself above every god, and shall speak marvellous things against the God of gods, and shall prosper till the indignation be accomplished: for that that is determined shall be done. Neither shall he regard the God of his fathers, nor the desire of women, nor regard any god: for he shall magnify himself above all. But in his estate shall he honour the God of forces: and a god whom his fathers knew not shall he honour with gold, and silver, and with precious stones, and pleasant things."

question: According to Daniel 11:41-45, what countries will escape his hand, where shall he plant the tabernacles of his palace, and what shall be his end?
opt1: Syria, Phoenicia, and the satrapies of Media will escape; he will build his pavilion upon Mount Hermon; and he shall be poisoned by his concubine
opt2: Philistia, Tyre, and the island of Cyprus will escape; he will pitch his tents in the valley of Jezreel; and he shall be slain by a Persian arrow
opt3: Egypt, Ethiopia, and Libya will escape; he will establish his headquarters at Mount Sinai; and an angel of God will strike him with leprosy
opt4: Edom, Moab, and the chief of the children of Ammon shall escape; he shall plant the tabernacles of his palace between the seas in the glorious holy mountain; yet he shall come to his end, and none shall help him
correct: Edom, Moab, and the chief of the children of Ammon shall escape; he shall plant the tabernacles of his palace between the seas in the glorious holy mountain; yet he shall come to his end, and none shall help him
explanation: Daniel 11:41, 45 (KJV) - "He shall enter also into the glorious land, and many countries shall be overthrown: but these shall escape out of his hand, even Edom, and Moab, and the chief of the children of Ammon ... And he shall plant the tabernacles of his palace between the seas in the glorious holy mountain; yet he shall come to his end, and none shall help him."

question: In Daniel 12:1, who stands up at that apocalyptic time for the children of Daniel's people, what unprecedented tribulation ensues, and who shall be delivered?
opt1: Gabriel shall blow the great trumpet of judgment; a fiery earthquake shall shake the foundations of the earth; and only the priests of Aaron shall be spared
opt2: The Messiah shall descend upon Mount Zion with twelve legions of angels; three days of darkness shall cover the nations; and all circumcision shall be preserved
opt3: David the king shall arise to shepherd the scattered flock; seven plagues shall consume Babylon; and the hundred and forty-four thousand shall escape
opt4: Michael shall stand up, the great prince which standeth for the children of thy people; there shall be a time of trouble such as never was since there was a nation; and at that time thy people shall be delivered, every one found written in the book
correct: Michael shall stand up, the great prince which standeth for the children of thy people; there shall be a time of trouble such as never was since there was a nation; and at that time thy people shall be delivered, every one found written in the book
explanation: Daniel 12:1 (KJV) - "And at that time shall Michael stand up, the great prince which standeth for the children of thy people: and there shall be a time of trouble, such as never was since there was a nation even to that same time: and at that time thy people shall be delivered, every one that shall be found written in the book."

question: What foundational doctrine of bodily resurrection and eternal destinies is explicitly unveiled in Daniel 12:2?
opt1: "And many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt"
opt2: "And all the souls of the righteous shall wander as disembodied spirits in the paradise of God forever"
opt3: "And the dead shall be reincarnated into new generations of Judah until seventy jubilees are fulfilled"
opt4: "And the wicked shall be annihilated into nothingness, while the righteous inherit the earthly cities of Palestine"
correct: "And many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt"
explanation: Daniel 12:2 (KJV) - "And many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt."

question: According to Daniel 12:3, what glorious reward and celestial radiance await the wise and those who turn many to righteousness?
opt1: They that endure shall wear crowns of fine gold and sit upon twelve ivory thrones judging the nations
opt2: They that be wise shall shine as the brightness of the firmament; and they that turn many to righteousness as the stars for ever and ever
opt3: They that fast shall drink from the river of life and feast upon the hidden manna in the heavenly sanctuary
opt4: They that teach the law shall be clothed in scarlet and walk with archangels through the streets of the new Jerusalem
correct: They that be wise shall shine as the brightness of the firmament; and they that turn many to righteousness as the stars for ever and ever
explanation: Daniel 12:3 (KJV) - "And they that be wise shall shine as the brightness of the firmament; and they that turn many to righteousness as the stars for ever and ever."

question: In Daniel 12:4, what instruction did the angel give to Daniel concerning the prophetic book, and what will characterize human activity in the time of the end?
opt1: "Inscribe the words upon tablets of stone and bury them in the cave of Machpelah: for nations shall war and kingdoms decay"
opt2: "Read the words aloud in the synagogues of Babylon: for the hearts of men shall grow cold and faith shall vanish from the earth"
opt3: "Shut up the words, and seal the book, even to the time of the end: many shall run to and fro, and knowledge shall be increased"
opt4: "Send copies of the book unto the four corners of the world: for false prophets shall arise and work lying wonders"
correct: "Shut up the words, and seal the book, even to the time of the end: many shall run to and fro, and knowledge shall be increased"
explanation: Daniel 12:4 (KJV) - "But thou, O Daniel, shut up the words, and seal the book, even to the time of the end: many shall run to and fro, and knowledge shall be increased."

question: According to Daniel 12:5-7, who stood on the banks of the river, and what solemn oath did the man clothed in linen sware by Him that liveth forever concerning the duration of these wonders?
opt1: Four cherubim stood on the riverbanks; the angel Gabriel held up a golden balance, swearing by the name of Jehovah that forty-two months were determined
opt2: The spirits of Moses and Elijah stood by the waters; a voice from heaven sware that after seventy weeks of days the sanctuary would be cleansed
opt3: Two watchers descended from the clouds; Michael drew his sword over the Hiddekel, swearing that within one thousand days Babylon would fall
opt4: Two others stood, one on this side of the bank of the river and the other on that side; the man in linen upon the waters held up his right hand and his left hand unto heaven, and sware that it shall be for a time, times, and an half; and when the power of the holy people is scattered, all these things shall be finished
correct: Two others stood, one on this side of the bank of the river and the other on that side; the man in linen upon the waters held up his right hand and his left hand unto heaven, and sware that it shall be for a time, times, and an half; and when the power of the holy people is scattered, all these things shall be finished
explanation: Daniel 12:5, 7 (KJV) - "Then I Daniel looked, and, behold, there stood other two, the one on this side of the bank of the river, and the other on that side of the bank of the river ... And I heard the man clothed in linen, which was upon the waters of the river, when he held up his right hand and his left hand unto heaven, and sware by him that liveth for ever that it shall be for a time, times, and an half; and when he shall have accomplished to scatter the power of the holy people, all these things shall be finished."

question: In Daniel 12:8-9, when Daniel heard the oath but understood not and asked what the end of these things should be, what was the angel's response?
opt1: "Go thy way, Daniel: for the words are closed up and sealed till the time of the end"
opt2: "Inquire of the elders of Judah: for they shall teach thee the mysteries of the kingdom"
opt3: "Fast for another twenty-one days: and the meaning of the time, times, and an half shall be shown unto thee"
opt4: "Weep not, O prophet: for the book will be opened by the lion of the tribe of Judah in the latter days"
correct: "Go thy way, Daniel: for the words are closed up and sealed till the time of the end"
explanation: Daniel 12:8-9 (KJV) - "And I heard, but I understood not: then said I, O my Lord, what shall be the end of these things? And he said, Go thy way, Daniel: for the words are closed up and sealed till the time of the end."

question: According to Daniel 12:10, what spiritual separation and moral refining process is foretold to occur among mankind?
opt1: All Israel will repent in sackcloth and be saved; while the Gentiles will blindly worship idols until the fire consumes them
opt2: Many shall be purified, and made white, and tried; but the wicked shall do wickedly: and none of the wicked shall understand; but the wise shall understand
opt3: The hypocrites will be exposed by seven angels; and the temple priests will perform daily purifications with the ashes of a red heifer
opt4: The righteous will be taken up into heaven in chariots; while the wicked will slay one another in the valley of decision
correct: Many shall be purified, and made white, and tried; but the wicked shall do wickedly: and none of the wicked shall understand; but the wise shall understand
explanation: Daniel 12:10 (KJV) - "Many shall be purified, and made white, and tried; but the wicked shall do wickedly: and none of the wicked shall understand; but the wise shall understand."

question: In Daniel 12:11, what exact number of days is specified from the time that the daily sacrifice is removed and the abomination of desolation set up?
opt1: A thousand two hundred and sixty days

opt4: A thousand three hundred and thirty-five days
correct: A thousand two hundred and ninety days
explanation: Daniel 12:11 (KJV) - "And from the time that the daily sacrifice shall be taken away, and the abomination that maketh desolate set up, there shall be a thousand two hundred and ninety days."

question: According to Daniel 12:12, what beatitude is pronounced upon the faithful believer, and to what specific number of days does he attain?
opt1: "Blessed is he that keepeth his garments clean, and cometh to the thousand two hundred days"

opt4: "Blessed is he that waiteth, and cometh to the thousand three hundred and five and thirty days"

explanation: Daniel 12:12 (KJV) - "Blessed is he that waiteth, and cometh to the thousand three hundred and five and thirty days."

question: What gracious personal promise and eternal destiny does the Lord bestow upon Daniel in the concluding verse of the book, Daniel 12:13?
opt1: "But go thou thy way till the end be: for thou shalt rest, and stand in thy lot at the end of the days"
opt2: "Return now unto Jerusalem in peace: for thou shalt see the foundation of the second temple laid before thou diest"
